page: Vultr vcg-a40-4c-20g-8vram is a fractional GPU instance belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features 4 vCPUs allocated on a shared Intel x86_64 processor with 2 physical cores, 2 threads per core, and a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. System memory consists of 20.0 GB RAM, providing 5.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a fractional 0.1667 NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU equipped with 8 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 360 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear division between general compute and specialized workloads. The instance achieves top-tier results in LLM inference, processing 9881.81 tokens per second for prompt processing and 465.27 tokens per second for text generation on a small 135M model. For a medium 7B model, it maintains top-tier performance with 3161.22 tokens per second for prompt processing and 107.91 tokens per second for text generation. Conversely, general CPU and memory tasks fall into the average range, with a Passmark CPU score of 7273.24 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7057.24.

Tradeoffs are evident in multi-threaded decompression and database operations. The instance registered a poor result in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and weak performance in Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput. These metrics indicate that while the fractional GPU is highly efficient for lightweight AI inference and machine learning tasks, the shared CPU architecture and lower single-core performance make it less suitable for high-throughput database hosting or heavy multi-threaded CPU-bound processing. The hardware profile is best optimized for small-scale LLM deployment, model prototyping, and GPU-assisted development workloads.

It features 4 shared Intel x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 20.0 GB of RAM, and a 360 GB NVMe SSD. Graphics acceleration is provided by a fractional 0.1667 NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in LLM inference for both small and medium models, while general CPU and database operations perform in the average to weak ranges. This resource profile makes the instance highly cost-efficient for lightweight machine learning inference, model prototyping, and GPU-accelerated development, though it is less suited for heavy database operations or intensive multi-threaded CPU tasks.
